subject: Nanotechnology
title: Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors
description: A 60-second lesson on Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors.

hook.text: Conventional transistors cannot switch faster than a thermal limit — tunnel FETs break through it.

buildup.text: A MOSFET's subthreshold swing is limited to 60 mV per decade at room temperature by Boltzmann statistics.

discovery.text: TFETs use band-to-band tunneling instead of thermal emission — enabling steeper switching slopes.

twist.text: Steeper slopes mean lower operating voltage — and exponentially lower power consumption.

climax.text: Real TFETs struggle with low drive current — the very tunneling that helps switching also limits throughput.

punchline.text: Tunnel through the barrier and break the switching speed limit.

quiz.question: What advantage do tunnel FETs have over conventional MOSFETs?
options: They can switch at lower voltages due to steeper subthreshold swing
